reasons: No insurance provision exists anywhere in the Agreement, and Kubient is a hosting vendor that collects, maintains and stores visitor data (p0035), so the 'missing' classification and insertion are correct under the rule's detection guidance (walk-away: no insurance for a vendor processing personal data).

The inserted paragraph tracks the model language at the preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Customer/visitor data is processed, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request) and is appropriately placed at the end of the General Provisions section, leaving existing text untouched — a minimal, additive edit.

The comment accurately states the gap, explains what was added, and offers the playbook fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) in the prescribed concise first-person-plural tone with the correct prefix.

Minor, non-disqualifying nits: the inserted paragraph is not lettered '(j)' as the rationale describes, and it relies on capitalized 'Term' and 'Law' which may not be defined terms in this Agreement — worth a conforming tidy-up but neither affects substance.
